Simultaneously start the web UI server, scheduler, and optionally coordinator in a single command.
This convenience command combines the functionality of 'dagu server', 'dagu scheduler',
and optionally 'dagu coordinator' into a single process. The web UI provides the management
interface, the scheduler handles automated DAG-run execution based on defined schedules,
and the coordinator (when enabled) manages distributed task execution across workers.
The coordinator is enabled by default and can be disabled by setting coordinator.enabled=false
in the config file or DAGU_COORDINATOR_ENABLED=false as an environment variable.
  --coordinator.host string         Host address to bind the coordinator gRPC server to (default: 127.0.0.1)
  --coordinator.advertise string    Address to advertise in service registry (default: auto-detected hostname)
  --coordinator.port int            Port number for the coordinator gRPC server (default: 50055)
  # Default mode (coordinator enabled)
  # Disable coordinator
  DAGU_COORDINATOR_ENABLED=false dagu start-all
  # Distributed mode with coordinator on all interfaces
  dagu start-all --coordinator.host=0.0.0.0 --coordinator.port=50055
  # Production with both web and coordinator on all interfaces
  dagu start-all --host=0.0.0.0 --port=8080 --coordinator.host=0.0.0.0
  -A, --coordinator.advertise string   Address to advertise in service registry (default: auto-detected hostname)
  -H, --coordinator.host string        Coordinator gRPC server host (default: 127.0.0.1) (default "127.0.0.1")
  -P, --coordinator.port string        Coordinator gRPC server port (default: 50055) (default "50055")

native_choices.checked: Native ecal CLI, native is_session/session_close and Dagu preconditions/retries/handlers.
native_choices.why: ecal renders a calendar; compose native session/close queries into the job eligibility/input-mtime token and leave skipping to Dagu.

native_choices.checked: restic stdin-from-command, SQLite CLI .backup/.dump, SQLite sqlite3_rsync, CPython Online Backup and subprocess timeout.
native_choices.why: Native operations do the copying/backups/checks/restores; consumer glue freezes the external oracle and required tables, rotates checks with a deadline and refuses controls.
Replace exclusive-create sentinels with nonblocking process-owned flock; stale file survives safely and no custom stale-lock recovery runs.

native_choices.checked: systemd Restart=on-failure, Dagu native history/status and native handlers/retries.
native_choices.why: Upstreams own supervision and run records; identity/time/holiday guards and exact due-slot correlation are our acceptance procedure.

native_choices.checked: Native Online Backup, restic backup/check/restore and .backup/.dump/sqlite3_rsync alternatives.
native_choices.why: Synthetic concurrent WAL writers, failures preserving integrity/counts and path-free integration evidence are consumer acceptance rather than replacement backup tools.

stdin_assessment.backup: restic stores command stdout; sqlite3 .backup writes a destination DB and emits no DB stdout, so this command would archive an empty stream.
stdin_assessment.dump: Logical SQL dump would require replay and a different completeness oracle; this contract freezes staged binary DB inventory before restic.
stdin_assessment.maintained_tool: SQLite upstream sqlite3_rsync performs live replication; it does not replace the encrypted restic repository/consumer-oracle contract.

retained_decision.rule: Keep restic and stdlib Online Backup; independent destination, key recovery and second-host consumer restore are decision 3.
